prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production game environment floor texture ONLY, no room, no walls, no furniture. Required output resolution 3840x2160 pixels (4K landscape), detailed native-resolution ink/paint edges; this must cover a 2880x1620 game map by DOWNSCALING, never upscaling. Fill entire frame edge to edge with individually hand-painted flat cut flagstones in a medieval underground tavern. A near-topdown 2D game view with vertical compression (stone height 0.5 to 0.8 of width). Approximately 55-65 irregular stones across the entire image width, widths around 55-105px at 3840 output; mixed angular quadrilaterals and pentagons, some larger rectangles and small repairs. Critically NO long horizontal rows, NO running bond brickwork, NO horizontal mortar line longer than 3 stones. Each stone's north/south boundary at a different height to neighbors; broken irregular staggered puzzle-like flagstone paving, not a wall, not round cobbles, not a Voronoi pebble carpet. Thin crisp dark 1-2 final-pixel joints. Shallow flat matte surfaces, not inflated pillows, not outlined bevel highlights. Delicate dark brown ink-like edges with restrained clear cel painting compatible with a nonpixel illustrated fantasy game. Low saturation warm gray-brown stone, reference colors faces RGB 77,70,60 and grout 48,43,36, overall grayscale mean about 65-70. Small subtle variations between stones with local standard deviation 6-12. Even diffuse albedo lighting across whole image, no directional cast shadows, no baked light bloom, no vignette, no lamps, no moss, no plants, no green or blue, no saturated red, no fine noisy grain. Smooth worn surfaces with broad restrained brushwork, no random decorative scratches on every stone. Three scattered irregular dark brown damp traces (not round stains, no shine) and only 2-3 small cracked slabs. A few subtly different replaced stones. Do not repeat any patch. No text, no border. CRISP but understated, floor behind 135px tall humans should not compete with characters.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the shown floor texture as a style reference but make paving stones MUCH SMALLER, approximately one THIRD their current width and height. A dense broad expanse with at least 36-40 small flagstones across 1672 image pixels, about 40-65 pixel wide small angular flat paving slabs, vertical heights 25-45px. Show the floor from near overhead with slight vertical compression. CRITICAL all joints stagger irregularly in both axes, no horizontal courses, no row extends farther than three slabs. Mixed quadrilaterals/pentagons and some small rectangles fitted like masonry puzzle, no round cobbles, not a wall. Pale delicate brown-black line joins 1-2px thin, subdued flat matte cel-painted broad surfaces with grayscale average around 68, warm low-saturation taupe-gray RGB about75,68,59. Very restrained stone variation, no harsh bevels or shiny pillow highlights, no noisy scratches, avoid orange/green/blue. Entire image uniform albedo, no gradients, no light bloom or cast shadows. Three SMALL sparse irregular brown damp traces and only two small cracked stones, not cracks everywhere. No other objects, no wall, no text, no border. Crisp native pixel edges, never blur. One continuous unique field, no texture repetition. Output 1672x941 landscape.

Bottom left: a small medieval dark wrought iron rectangular floor drain grate seen from overhead with vertical compression 0.65, simple 5 dark crossbars in plain square rim, zero gold or shine. Bottom right: ONE replacement flat irregular pentagonal stone, slightly lighter warm gray-brown with thin dark edge, no crack, no bevel. Art matches understated hand-painted 2D nonpixel medieval underground tavern paving, delicate lines and soft clear cel painting. No floor background behind items, no shadow outside items, no text, no labels, no UI, no circles. All items mutually separated and within their own 3x2 cell.
